rows.behavior_contract: Before each AI phase/worker, classify the whole assignment from actual scope/evidence; medium is routine execution only, xhigh is the default for planning/implementation/review/evidence/judgment/diagnosis/convergence/stateful performer work, and high requires a concrete inspected-scope reason. Preserve completed evidence when failures or complexity force escalation. On Codex review providers pin reuse/structure/performance lenses to gpt-6.1-sol with configured-model fallback recorded; all host adapters must use only supported effort/model controls and record inheritance/fallback honestly. Harness tasks whose code is not user-run pin all Codex review and assessment leaves to gpt-6.1-sol while leaving implementation/other phases on the configured model; unavailable pins fall back with evidence.
rows.state_machine: inspect complete scope/current evidence -> select medium|high|xhigh -> record reason -> apply supported host setting or inheritance fallback -> execute phase -> if failure/complexity exceeds class preserve valid outputs -> escalate medium/high to xhigh (or justified high from medium) -> retain review/evidence contract -> re-evaluate before new child scope
side_effects: Repository workflow/test/evidence governance only; no new shipping runtime.
failure_cases: medium selected for work containing planning, repair, judgment or synthesis
high selected without a concrete inspected-scope reason
failure diagnosis/repair continues at medium instead of escalating
unexpected complexity remains high instead of escalating to xhigh
valid prior artifacts/checks discarded solely because effort changes
reuse/structure/performance Codex lens silently omits gpt-6.1-sol pin or fallback record
host adapter invents unsupported effort/model arguments
prompt wording is claimed to change effort without a real host setting
extra CLI process/global setting/worker or stateful-performer replacement is introduced solely to tune effort/model
rows.ui_disposition: Not applicable; repository workflow governance only.
non_ui_responsibilities: selected effort/reason and applied/inherited setting recording
reuse/structure/performance gpt-6.1-sol pin and configured-model fallback
Claude supported model mapping without fictional reasoning field
new-scope re-evaluation without replacing stateful performer solely for tuning

rows.behavior_contract: The local video CLI supports probe, extract and sheet for supplied video files. Probe records the input SHA-256 and byte size plus codec, dimensions, duration, frame count, per-frame timestamps and frame-interval facts, so variable-frame-rate media is not reduced to nominal FPS. Extract validates selected frame indices and crop syntax, builds an ffmpeg filter chain, decodes with passthrough frame timing, requires the decoded count to equal the selected count, and names retained frames with source index/time provenance. Sheet uses Pillow to create a labelled contact sheet and rejects selections above 200 frames. Intermediate decoded frames are scoped to TemporaryDirectory; the helper does not upload media or own a persistent resource store.
rows.state_machine: SKILL.md conditionally invokes probe/extract/sheet for supplied video -> ffprobe enumerates stream/frame timing -> SHA-256/size and metadata are reported -> requested frame/range/crop/scale is parsed -> ffmpeg decodes selected frames into TemporaryDirectory -> extract moves frames to the explicit output path or sheet assembles a bounded Pillow contact sheet -> JSON output is emitted -> temporary intermediates are removed. Missing tools, invalid ranges/crops, no decoded frames or count mismatch fail. Empty selections are not explicitly rejected by this source and can cause an unhandled IndexError in extract/sheet.
side_effects: Reads the supplied local video and computes its digest/size during probe.
Writes extracted frames or a contact-sheet image only to the caller-selected output path.
Deletes intermediate decoded frames when TemporaryDirectory exits; no network upload or persistent product resource store is created.
failure_cases: ffprobe or ffmpeg is unavailable on PATH.
Pillow is unavailable for sheet generation.
The input has no video frames or lacks expected stream/format metadata.
Requested frame indices are negative or beyond the frame count.
Crop syntax does not match WxH+X+Y.
ffmpeg decodes a different frame count than requested.
An empty frame selection is not explicitly rejected and can reach unhandled IndexError in extract/sheet; a local equivalent would need a focused negative test and explicit failure behavior.

rows.behavior_contract: Treat cross-provider review as a developer review/evidence workflow over one frozen change scope: produce immutable per-round snapshots, run fresh blind read-only reviewers, synthesize and independently arbitrate every finding before edits, preserve reversal history, apply only accepted fixes, and re-review focused deltas until convergence or an explicit bounded stop without creating a second shipping review/runtime owner.

side_effects: Developer tooling may create ignored review-session snapshots, reviewer transcripts/reports and a durable per-session arbitration ledger outside the shipping product.
Accepted FIX decisions may edit the reviewed working tree only after the finding is durably arbitrated; review-only mode does not edit.

Fresh/read-only reviewers and synthesis may run concurrently only within the existing repository review lifecycle; the runner remains the sole stateful arbiter.

Provider launch completion is mistaken for reviewer completion, or a failed/incomplete report is accepted as evidence.

fabushi_target_symbols: A rebase is an Integrate/Deliver operation on one current Git worktree, not an ordinary product task, repository task queue item, or shipping runtime. Resolve the requested target and replay range to exact commits, record `OLD_TIP`, `ONTO`, and exclusive `REPLAY_BASE`, show the replay list and likely conflict surface, and stop when ambiguous interpretations would replay different commits. Remote-tracking refs are local snapshots and must not be refreshed without explicit authorization.

Branch and worktree ownership is fail-closed. Do not rebase a branch checked out in another worktree, mutate sibling worktrees, silently stash a dirty tree, create backup refs when reflog preserves the prior tip, or automatically push or force-push rewritten history. Resume or abort an already-active rebase rather than nesting another operation, and keep the operation non-interactive.

Resolve conflicts by intent, not textual side selection. For overlapping logic, orient the merge stages, read the replayed commit and surrounding series plus the competing base-side history, state both intents, and reapply the moved change in the current code shape. Review rerere-applied resolutions; skip an empty commit only after proving its intended state already exists. Never use whole-file ours/theirs selection, delete a hard hunk merely to pass, skip a hard conflict, or guess through a genuine semantic contradiction.

Verify each resolved conflict and the whole rewritten series. The completed rebase must use `git range-diff` over the original and rewritten ranges plus final branch log/status to account for every replayed or deliberately empty commit. Any executable Fabushi build/test verification runs only in exact-head GitHub Actions; upstream host-specific local compile commands are not Fabushi acceptance authority. Report the exact rebase command, `OLD_TIP` undo path, replayed/skipped commits with evidence, each conflict's competing intents and resolution, decisions, and lower-confidence results. A later force-push may be required for an already-published branch, but this workflow never performs it automatically.

rows.behavior_contract: Retain the exact precondition/postcondition contract proved by the locked Microsoft/GSL assertion tests without shipping a GSL-shaped assertion runtime. Expects and Ensures both evaluate the supplied condition and do nothing on the likely-true path; a false condition calls gsl::details::terminate(), which is noreturn/noexcept and uses std::terminate() in the normal configuration or the explicit MSVC no-exceptions/kernel workaround. The tests prove a valid Expects call returns its value, a false precondition terminates, a valid Ensures call returns after the postcondition, and a false postcondition terminates. Accepted tdesktop production code uses Expects/Ensures broadly, so this row closes only dependency test provenance and never bulk-closes caller responsibilities.
rows.state_machine: No independent long-lived state machine. Per contract check: evaluate caller-owned condition -> likely true => continue with no helper state -> false => gsl::details::terminate() -> standard std::terminate path or configured MSVC no-exceptions/kernel fail-fast path. Expects labels a precondition and Ensures labels a postcondition, but both share the same fail-closed check primitive.
side_effects: True contract checks have no helper-owned state or persistence side effect.
A false contract check transfers control to a noreturn termination path rather than returning success or a recoverable value.
Compiler suppression/branch-hint helpers and GSL_ASSUME do not create product state, persistence, network, UI or service side effects.
failure_cases: Weakening a false Expects/Ensures condition into a debug-only or ignored check.
Using GSL_ASSUME or an optimizer hint as if it validated untrusted/runtime state.
Inventing a GSLAssertionRuntime or global validation owner instead of keeping each production invariant with its actual Fabushi domain owner.

rows.behavior_contract: Retain the exact bounds-checked indexing contract proved by the locked Microsoft/GSL at tests without shipping a GSL-shaped indexing runtime. gsl::at requires i >= 0 and i < size/extent before indexing. The tests prove valid indices preserve the referenced element for built-in arrays, std::array, std::vector and std::span, preserve values for initializer_list, reject negative and end-boundary indices by contract death, and support constexpr access for the covered forms. rows.state_machine: No long-lived helper state. Built-in arrays also reject extents beyond ptrdiff_t representability at compile time.
side_effects: Valid at() access returns the same element/reference identity for mutable/const array/container/span forms tested.
initializer_list access returns the selected value after the same signed bounds check.

rows.behavior_contract: Retain the exact test-harness contract of Microsoft/GSL deathTestCommon.h without creating a shipping assertion or termination runtime. GetExpectedDeathString returns "Expected Death" when a terminate handler is available and ".*" only when setting the terminate handler failed. Exactly seven pinned GSL test source blobs include and call the helper and are registered in the shared gsl_tests target. tdesktop has zero direct helper/function consumers; no product responsibility is closed transitively.
rows.state_machine: No independent long-lived state machine. For each death assertion, the test harness supplies a terminate handler; if non-null the helper selects the stable expected-death matcher, otherwise it selects the fallback regex used to avoid a false-negative caused by handler installation failure. GTest and each test own assertion execution; the helper owns no product state.
side_effects: The helper performs only a constexpr pointer selection for the test matcher.
No persistence, network, UI, account, authorization, product runtime, or service side effect exists.
